newsitem.title: USA: U.S. says no interim refits needed for tankers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says no interim refits needed for tankers.

text.p: The U.S. Coast Guard ruled Friday that single hull tankers and barges would need no retrofits to prevent oil spills before they are retired or rebuilt to meet double hull requirements by 2015.
"The Coast Guard has determined that structural measures are not economically feasible," it said in a final rule under the Oil Pollution Act of 1990.

The agency weighed several factors, including the costs of construction, insurance, lost tonnage, and consumer impacts, and took into account that less oil had been spilled by tankers since the law was passed.
Under the 1990 law, all tankers operating in U.S. waters must be double-hulled by 2015.
But to help limit spills before the phase-out of single hull vessels was completed, Congress asked the Coast Guard to order additional protections.
Earlier this year, the agency issued a rule designed to reduce human error and the risk of accidents caused by equipment or structural failures.
The Coast Guard said those steps and oil spill emergency rules issued earlier should be adequate to protect U.S. waters until all tankers were double-hulled.
